declared_changes.mode: Replace host top-k with exact hierarchical device selection while retaining exhaustive forward scoring.
declared_changes.selection: Add 256-thread repeated reduction and recursive local-winner merging; support k=0..128 explicitly.
declared_changes.transfer: Only min(k,N) 24-byte winner records are copied inside retrieval boundary; optional dense validation copy remains outside.
declared_changes.warmup: Zero warmup queries and one observation/query: correctness validation only, no latency comparison.
declared_changes.runtime_gate: Report actual selection threads, supported k, merge levels, scratch bytes, verify flag, warmups/repeats and semantic marks; existing callers use empty extension defaults.
declared_changes.input_validation: Reject duplicate original IDs and malformed/duplicate/out-of-cap32 prepared query terms before measurement.

measurement: Correctness only; diagnostic stage/query times are not a speedup claim. Query boundary includes weight preparation/upload, scoring, all selection levels and top-k result copy. Excludes index upload, gate, CPU reference, validation-only dense copy and file writes.
success_rule: Zero GPU/Python fixture discrepancies and zero common-data full-score/top-k mismatches; fresh GPU TSVs must equal the historical canonical CPU outputs.
failure_rule: Preserve failed attempt; separately review any correction before retry.
next_if_success: Use this as ranking control for a separately branched same-layout block-exhaustive GPU control, then pruning.
unsupported: k>128 is rejected; k1000, batch and other layout algorithms are later work.
